LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 10.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Festivals Suggested vocabulary wedding, birthday, Christmas, Easter, Idd, Diwali
Topic 10.1: Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Festivals Suggested vocabulary wedding, birthday, Christmas, Easter, Idd, Diwali in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we learn new words? 2. How can we pronounce words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Listen to a text and point out words featuring the target letter- sound combinations:- mb, - nt, -nd, -nch. Learners with speech difficulties can point out orally, by typing or writing.

2. Practise saying words with the target letter-sound combinations, with peers.

3. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

4. Recite rhyming words that have the target letter- sound combinations. Learners with speech difficulties could use 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Listen to a text and point out words featuring the target letter- sound combinations:- mb, - nt, -nd, -nch. Learners with speech difficulties can point out orally, by typing or writing.
2. Practise saying words with the target letter-sound combinations, with peers.
3. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.
4. Recite rhyming words that have the target letter- sound combinations. Learners with speech difficulties could use 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: The learner’s ability to listen keenly and actively is enhanced as they listen to a text and point out words

featuring the target-letter sound combinations.

Collaboration: Teamwork is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively with peers to develop a talking tree observing the

rules of engagement.

Link to

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates the effort of peers in constructing sentences and gives positive feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they respond to three- directional instructions appropriately
